editorial:
Seventeen years after sparing the man who killed his son, former cop Leo Barnes now protects Senator Charlene Roan, who wants to end the Purge forever. When a government betrayal forces them onto the streets during the final Purge night, you get a tense, action-packed ride through a city gone wild. The movie mixes political drama with survival horror, giving you a front-row seat to chaos, masked killers, and a fight for the future of the country.

The action scenes are fast and brutal, and Frank Grillo brings real grit to Barnes. Elizabeth Mitchell is solid as Roan, though some side characters feel thin. The pacing rarely slows down, which keeps you hooked, but the dialogue can be cheesy at times. If you enjoy loud, violent thrillers with a political edge, this one delivers. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: Roan wins the election and officially ends the Purge, but the final twist reveals the New Founding Fathers refuse to accept defeat. A group of loyalists launches a last-minute attack to assassinate her, but Barnes and his allies fight them off in a brutal showdown. Roan survives, the Purge is abolished, and the country begins to heal, though the lingering threat of future violence remains.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves action thrillers with a political edge.
